column2: How do I install the full pack or the Europe pack of the weather?
column3: Settings → “🌦 Weather of the past”: an “📦 Install” button for each pack (base, Europe, full). The app downloads the pack from the project’s data page, in pieces: a bar shows the progress, “⏸ Pause” stops it and it picks up where it left off, even after you close the app. Then it checks it (its fingerprint) and installs it, with “↶ Undo”. No weather comes with the app: only what is needed to download it. Without internet, “Import a file…” takes a .lcmeteo file you have already downloaded or made (how-to: docs/METEO.md). “🗑 Delete the pack” removes it (with “↶ Undo”). “↗ About the data” gives each source and its licence.

column2: How do I send a map or a retouched image to Video editing or the Animation studio?
column3: In the vector drawing tool or in photo retouching: File → “📤 Send to Video editing or the Animation studio…”. Choose a new edit, an existing edit, a new Studio film or an existing film: the image is stored in the media and placed on the timeline (or as a new scene of the film).

column2: Was my family part of a great population movement (rural exodus, emigration…)?
column3: Lists → History → “🌍 Your family in the great movements”. The app compares each person’s moves (birth, baptism, marriage, residence, death…) with 32 great migrations in history, each with its source: rural exodus to Paris, people from Auvergne and Aveyron in Paris, Bretons, masons from the Creuse, Barcelonnettes in Mexico, Basques in the Americas, Italians, Poles, Spaniards, Portuguese, pieds-noirs, the 1940 exodus… Same departure, same arrival, same period: “Sure” or “Possible”, never forced on you. “Yes, that’s it” confirms it, “No” removes it (with “↶ Undo”). “🗺 On the migration map” opens a map of these journeys, ready to keep. On the profile, the “🌍 The world around” block says it too: “Pierre was part of: …”.

column2: How do I add a population movement I know about?
column3: Lists → History → “🌍 Your family in the great movements” → “＋ Add a movement”: its name (“The glassworkers of Carmaux to Albi”), its years, where people left from and where they went (department numbers, towns or countries, separated by commas), what you should know and its source. The app immediately looks for who in your family was part of it. ✎ edits it, 🗑 deletes it (with “↶ Undo”).

column2: How do I find out if an ancestor died during an epidemic (cholera, smallpox…)?
column3: Lists → History → “Epidemics, wars, terrible winters”. The crises of all of France and, on top of that, local crises (1832 cholera in Paris, 1813-1814 typhus in the East, 1875 Garonne flood, Courrières disaster…), each with its source, next to your family’s deaths in the same place at the same time. If the cause is written down (on the death, in its note, or in a transcribed record linked to the person: “died of cholera”, “died of the smallpox”), the app shows it and the death becomes “sure”; “Note as cause of death” keeps it on the death (with “↶ Undo”). For each crisis: the deaths month by month (the cholera summer, the flu winter) and children under 5 shown separately.

column2: How do I add a local crisis (fire, flood, epidemic in the village)?
column3: Lists → History → “🌍 The world around” → “＋ New event”, with the type “Epidemic”, “Famine”, “Terrible winter”, “War” or “Crisis”: it also goes into “Epidemics, wars, terrible winters” and into the “Births and deaths” chart. A single list of crises is used everywhere in the app.

column2: How do I see what time it is in other cities (world clocks)?
column3: Lists → Research and organisation → “🕰 World times”: “＋ Add a city” (more than 200 cities, or any time zone, or a city of your own). Each clock shows the time, day or night, and the difference from the time here. “⇄ Compare” puts the cities side by side: click a time here, and its column shows the time in each city (green from 8:00 to 20:00, grey at night). “🎨 Style” sets everything: hands or digits, dial shape, colours, seconds, date.

column2: How do I see the time zone map, and who has which time?
column3: World times → “🗺 Time zone map”: each country at its legal time today (summer time included), large countries split into regions (United States, Canada, Russia, Brazil, Australia…), night shown as a shadow; hover over a country to see its time zone. “Theoretical time zones” shows the 15° bands. “🎨 Time zone colours”: ready-made sets (cold to warm, rainbow, pastel, two-tone school atlas…) or a colour of your own for each time zone. At the bottom, “📋 Which countries and regions for each time zone” shows or hides the list, with a search.

column2: How do I put clocks on the dashboard?
column3: Dashboard → “✎ Customise” → add the “🕰 World clocks” widget. In its settings: the cities to show (empty: those of the World times list) and a style of its own (hands or digits, dial, colours); otherwise it uses the list’s style.

column2: What are the sums and measures written in a record worth today?
column3: In the Transcription workshop, sums (“three hundred livres tournois”, “twelve livres ten sols”) and measures (“one and a half arpents”, “five pieds two pouces”) are underlined in green. Hover over them: the sum in today’s euros (based on the year of the record), in kilos of bread and in days of a day labourer’s work; the measure in metres, ares or litres, using the tables of the region where the record was made, with the source. “See the calculation” opens the 🪙 Old money converter, with the sourced prices of that year. Post-mortem inventories also give “≈ € today” for each object and for the total. The Workshop bar setting “Old sums and measures underlined” turns them off.
